# `silk/mem/frozen`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Shared ownership of one value that never changes, on one thread, with plain shared borrows.

## When to use
Use [`Frozen`](#Frozen) when many owners hold the same value and only read it, such as the nodes of a
hash-consed tree. Equal values can then share one allocation, and code can read two handles to
the same value at once. For a value that changes, use `silk.mem.shared.Shared`.

## Details
[`Frozen.make`](#Frozen.impl.make) allocates one time. [`Frozen.clone`](#Frozen.impl.clone), [`Frozen.with`](#Frozen.impl.with) and [`Frozen.get`](#Frozen.impl.get) do not
allocate. The value is dropped when the last handle is dropped. A handle stays on the thread that
made it; share across threads with `silk.concurrency.sync.Arc`.

Unlike `Shared`, access is not exclusive: a nested read of the same value through any handle is
allowed, since no handle can change it.

## Gotchas
Handles that refer to each other in a cycle are never dropped. A value that never changes cannot
form a cycle unless it held a mutable handle, such as a `Shared`, that was changed later.

## Examples
### Read one value through two handles at once
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.mem.frozen { Frozen }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let first = run Frozen<i32>.make(40) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let second = Frozen<i32>.clone(&first)
  let sum = Frozen<i32>.with<i32>(&first, fn(left: &i32) -> i32 {
    return Frozen<i32>.with<i32>(&second, fn(right: &i32) -> i32 { return left.* + right.* })
  })
  if sum != 80 || Frozen<i32>.count(&first) != 2 { return 1 }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `Frozen` with `import silk.mem.frozen { Frozen }`.

<a id="Frozen"></a>

## `Frozen`

```silk
pub struct Frozen<T>
```

A handle to one value of type `T` that never changes and that other handles can also own.

### Details

The handle is one pointer. Its count is a plain word, so a handle cannot move to another thread.
[`Frozen.with`](#Frozen.impl.with) and [`Frozen.get`](#Frozen.impl.get) give shared borrows only, and any number of them can be live
at once, also to the same value.

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub effect<'env> fn make<'env>(value: T) -> Frozen<T> ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Allocates storage, moves `value` into it, and returns the first handle.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the storage. `value` is dropped.

<a id="Frozen.impl.clone"></a>

### Method `clone`

```silk
pub fn clone(self: &Self) -> Frozen<T>
```

Returns a new handle to the same value. It does not allocate and does not touch the value.

#### Gotchas

A count past half the range of a word traps before the handle exists.

<a id="Frozen.impl.get"></a>

### Method `get`

```silk
pub fn get<'a>(self: &'a Self) -> &'a T
```

Borrows the value for as long as this handle is borrowed.

<a id="Frozen.impl.with"></a>

### Method `with`

```silk
pub fn with<A>(self: &Self, use: once fn(&T) -> A) -> A
```

Calls `use` one time with a shared borrow of the value and returns the result of `use`.

#### Details

The callback can read this value again, through this handle or any other.

<a id="Frozen.impl.count"></a>

### Method `count`

```silk
pub fn count(self: &Self) -> usize
```

Returns the number of handles to the value.

<a id="Frozen.impl.address"></a>

### Method `address`

```silk
pub fn address(self: &Self) -> usize
```

The address of the value's allocation, which every handle to it shares. It stays the same
while any handle lives, and another value can reuse it after the last handle drops.

<a id="Frozen.impl.same"></a>

```silk
pub fn same(left: &Self, right: &Self) -> bool
```

Whether both handles refer to the same allocation, which equal values made apart do not.
